topic_ko: 초고층 건물의 와류 현상과 설계 대응 전략
_note: 삽입(논설·설명문) FULL set. 유형마다 passage를 다르게 패러프레이즈. grammar/vocab의 밑줄·blank_target·insert text는 해당 passage 문장에 글자 그대로 존재.

insert.insert_sentence: To minimize vortex shedding, skyscraper designers do everything in their powers to confuse the wind.

passage_marked.text: To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles.
As wind meets a rectangular skyscraper it pushes on the flat face of the building before flowing around its sides, where eventually it separates from the face of the structure.
The vortices pull and push the building in a direction perpendicular to the wind at frequencies that can become dangerously self-sustaining.
Orienting the building so that the longer face of the structure is parallel with prevailing winds can help.
Chopping or rounding off corners of a building can likewise make it more aerodynamic.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장('와류를 최소화하기 위해 설계자들이 바람을 교란하기 위한 모든 것을 한다')은 ③ 직전까지 와류의 생성과 위험성 설명이 끝난 뒤, ③ 이후에 나열되는 세 가지 구체적 대응책(방향 잡기·모서리 깎기·발코니 배치)을 도입하는 총론 문장이다. 따라서 ③이 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: ①은 직사각형 형태 서술 직후 — 와류 메커니즘 설명이 아직 시작조차 되지 않아 대응 총론이 오기에 지나치게 이르다. ②는 바람-건물 상호작용 설명 후 — 와류의 위험성(자기 지속적 주파수) 서술이 아직 끝나지 않았다. ④는 첫 번째 대응책(Orienting) 이후 — 총론이 구체 방법 중간에 끼어드는 논리 역전이다. ⑤는 두 번째 대응책 이후 — 마지막 대응책(Roughing up)이 뒤따르므로 총론의 자리가 아니다.

passage: Skyscrapers are commonly built as squares or rectangles because these shapes keep construction costs low and profits high.
However, such shapes are aerodynamically inefficient and lead to a hazardous wind effect known as vortex shedding.
When wind strikes the flat face of a rectangular tower, it travels around the sides before detaching from the surface.
This detachment creates a pressure imbalance that generates rotating columns of air — vortices — trailing behind the building.
These vortices exert sideways forces at rhythmic frequencies, and the oscillation can dangerously amplify itself.
To counter this, architects employ techniques aimed at disrupting the wind's ability to form coherent vortices.
One approach is to rotate the building so its long side faces the prevailing wind direction.
Another is to bevel, curve, or texture the corners using balconies and terraces to break up the spinning air.
choices: the financial reasons skyscrapers are built in rectangular form
engineering strategies used to reduce the dangerous effects of vortex shedding on skyscrapers
why wind speed increases at the corners of tall rectangular buildings
the history of aerodynamic research applied to urban architecture
how the height of a building determines the strength of vortex formation
theme.explanation_ko: 글은 초고층 건물의 직사각형 형태가 일으키는 와류 위험을 소개하고, 그것을 줄이기 위한 구체적 설계 전략을 설명한다. 이 전체를 아우르는 주제는 ②이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①재정적 이유, ③모서리 풍속 증가, ④공기역학 역사, ⑤높이와 와류 강도 관계는 모두 본문이 다루는 핵심 초점이 아니다.

passage: Rectangular forms dominate skyscraper design because they minimize material costs and maximize usable floor space.
Yet these same right-angled shapes are notorious for triggering an aerodynamic hazard called vortex shedding.
As airflow collides with a flat facade, it peels away at the edges, generating spinning eddies that trail downwind.
These eddies push and pull the tower sideways at frequencies that can escalate into destructive resonance.
Architects, therefore, treat the wind as an adversary to be outmaneuvered rather than simply resisted.
They orient the building's longer axis in line with dominant winds to reduce the face exposed to oncoming airflow.
They also shave or round the building's corners, depriving the wind of the sharp edges it needs to anchor strong vortices.
Finally, balconies and step-backs add surface texture that interrupts vortex formation before it can build momentum.
choices: The Hidden Costs of Skyscraper Construction
How Architects Tame the Wind Around Tall Buildings
Why Wind Speed Is Greatest at Building Corners
The Physics of Pressure Waves in Urban Canyons
Rectangular Buildings and Their Benefits for Urban Planning
title.explanation_ko: 건축가들이 와류 위험에 맞서 초고층 건물의 바람을 제어하는 설계 전략들을 다루므로, '건축가들이 고층 건물 주변의 바람을 어떻게 길들이는가'라는 ②가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①시공 비용, ③모서리 풍속, ④압력파 물리학, ⑤직사각형의 도시계획 이점은 본문의 핵심 논지와 다르다.

passage: To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles.
These are not particularly aerodynamic shapes, and this results in a wind phenomenon called "vortex shedding."
As wind meets a rectangular skyscraper it pushes on the flat face of the building before flowing around its sides, where eventually it separates from the face of the structure.
The difference in pressures on the front and back faces of the building gives rise to vortices, or spinning currents of wind, that flows downstream from the building.
The vortices pull and push the building in a direction perpendicular to the wind at frequencies that can become dangerously self-sustaining.
Orienting the building so that the longer face of the structure is parallel with prevailing winds can help.
Chopping or rounding off corners of a building can likewise make it more aerodynamic.
Roughing up the corners of the building through the careful placement of balconies or stepped corners can help by disturbing or delaying the formation of strong vortices.
grammar.explanation_ko: ③ 관계대명사절 'that flows downstream'에서 선행사는 복수명사 'vortices'이므로, 관계대명사절의 동사도 복수형 'flow'를 써야 한다. 'flows'는 단수 동사이므로 수 일치 오류 — 'that flow downstream'으로 고쳐야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① To minimize: 목적 to부정사 — 적절. ② flowing: before + 동명사 — 적절. ④ dangerously self-sustaining: 부사 + 형용사 — 적절. ⑤ Orienting: 동명사 주어 — 적절.

passage: To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles.
These are not particularly aerodynamic shapes, and this results in a wind phenomenon called "vortex shedding."
As wind meets a rectangular skyscraper it pushes on the flat face of the building before flowing around its sides, where eventually it separates from the face of the structure.

The vortices pull and push the building in a direction perpendicular to the wind at frequencies that can become dangerously self-sustaining.

Chopping or rounding off corners of a building can likewise make it less aerodynamic.

vocab.explanation_ko: ⑤ 모서리를 잘라내거나 둥글게 하면 건물이 '더 공기역학적(more aerodynamic)'이 되어 와류가 줄어드는 것이 글의 논지이다. 'less aerodynamic(덜 공기역학적)'은 반대 의미이므로 문맥상 틀리다 → more aerodynamic으로 고쳐야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① maximize(극대화하다), ② results in(초래하다), ③ downstream(하류 방향으로), ④ prevailing(지배적인)은 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles.
These are not particularly aerodynamic shapes, and this results in a dangerous wind effect called vortex shedding.
When wind meets a rectangular skyscraper, it pushes on the flat face before flowing around its sides, where it eventually separates from the structure.
This separation creates a pressure gap that generates spinning air currents — vortices — trailing behind the building.
These vortices push and pull the building sideways at frequencies that may become dangerously self-reinforcing.
To counter this, designers orient the building so its longer face is parallel with prevailing winds.
They also chop or round off corners to improve the building's aerodynamic profile.
In addition, balconies and stepped corners can disturb or delay the formation of powerful vortices.
blank.explanation_ko: 와류가 외부 자극 없이도 스스로 증폭되어 건물에 공명 진동을 일으킬 수 있다는 내용 — '위험할 정도로 자기 강화적인(dangerously self-reinforcing)'이 문맥에 맞다. 나머지는 모두 와류의 실제 위험성과 반대되는 의미.
blank.distractor_ko: ②안전하게 예측 가능, ③점차 약해지는, ④구조적으로 유익한, ⑤쉽게 관리 가능은 와류의 위험성과 반대 의미이다.

order.given: To minimize building costs and maximize revenues, skyscrapers generally take the shape of squares or rectangles. These are not particularly aerodynamic shapes, and this results in a wind phenomenon called "vortex shedding."

blocks.A: Orienting the building so that the longer face of the structure is parallel with prevailing winds can help. Chopping or rounding off corners of a building can likewise make it more aerodynamic, and roughing up the corners through the careful placement of balconies or stepped corners can help by disturbing or delaying the formation of strong vortices.
blocks.B: As wind meets a rectangular skyscraper it pushes on the flat face before flowing around its sides, where it separates from the structure. The difference in pressures gives rise to vortices — spinning currents — that flow downstream from the building.
blocks.C: The vortices pull and push the building in a direction perpendicular to the wind at frequencies that can become dangerously self-sustaining. To minimize vortex shedding, skyscraper designers do everything in their powers to confuse the wind.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글에서 와류 현상 용어가 도입된 뒤, (B)에서 바람-건물 상호작용 메커니즘과 와류 생성을 설명하고, (C)에서 와류의 위험성을 서술하고 '설계자들이 바람을 교란한다'는 대응 총론을 제시하며, (A)에서 세 가지 구체적 대응책(건물 방향 잡기·모서리 깎기·발코니 배치)을 나열한다. (B)-(C)-(A).
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 총론('confuse the wind')은 위험성 설명 직후 대응 의도를 선언하므로 (B) 뒤에 와야 하고, (A)의 구체 대응책들은 총론(C) 뒤에 열거되어야 한다. (A)를 먼저 놓으면 구체 방법이 총론보다 앞서 나오는 논리 역전이 된다.

passage: Rectangular skyscrapers are cost-efficient to build but aerodynamically problematic.
Their flat, angular surfaces cause a wind effect called vortex shedding.
Wind flowing around the building separates at its edges, generating spinning air currents behind the structure.
These vortices push the building sideways at self-reinforcing frequencies, posing a structural danger.
Designers respond by confusing the wind through multiple techniques.
Rotating the building so its longer face is parallel to prevailing winds reduces the area of direct impact.
Trimming or curving corners makes the profile more aerodynamic and disrupts orderly vortex formation.
Adding balconies or step-backs creates surface turbulence that delays the build-up of powerful vortices.
summary.summary_template: Rectangular skyscrapers are prone to __(A)__, a wind phenomenon that pushes buildings sideways at dangerous frequencies, so designers use several strategies to __(B)__ the wind and prevent the build-up of strong spinning currents.
summary.explanation_ko: (A) 직사각형 건물이 겪는 바람 현상 = 'vortex shedding(와류 현상)'. (B) 설계자들이 하는 것 = 'confuse(교란하다)' — 원문 주어진 문장의 핵심 동사. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A) wind resistance/pressure drop/aerodynamic lift는 본문의 핵심 용어가 아니다. (B) block/redirect/strengthen은 원문 'confuse the wind'와 다르거나 반대 의미이다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 건물의 더 긴 면이 지배적인 바람의 방향과 평행하도록 건물의 방향을 잡는 것이 도움이 될 수 있다.
writing.answer: Orienting the building so that the longer face of the structure is parallel with prevailing winds can help.
writing.explanation_ko: 동명사 Orienting이 주어, so that + 절로 목적 서술, parallel with prevailing winds.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 건물의 전면과 후면의 기압 차이는 건물로부터 하류 방향으로 흐르는 와류를 만들어낸다.
writing.answer: The difference in pressures on the front and back faces of the building gives rise to vortices that flow downstream from the building.
writing.explanation_ko: give rise to(야기하다), 주격 관계대명사 that flow downstream.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 와류 현상을 최소화하기 위해, 초고층 건물 설계자들은 바람을 교란하기 위해 자신들이 할 수 있는 모든 것을 한다.
conditions: do everything in their powers를 포함할 것
to confuse the wind로 목적을 나타낼 것
writing.answer: To minimize vortex shedding, skyscraper designers do everything in their powers to confuse the wind.
writing.explanation_ko: To minimize(목적 to부정사) + 주어 + do everything in their powers(관용 표현) + to confuse(목적).

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: Roughing up the corners of the building through the careful placement of balconies or stepped corners can help by disturbing or delaying the formation of strong vortices.
writing.answer: 발코니나 단차진 모서리의 신중한 배치를 통해 건물의 모서리를 거칠게 만드는 것은 강한 와류의 형성을 방해하거나 지연시킴으로써 도움이 될 수 있다.
writing.explanation_ko: Roughing up(동명사 주어 — 거칠게 만드는 것), through the careful placement of(~의 배치를 통해), by disturbing or delaying(~함으로써).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: The vortices pull and push the building in a direction _______________ to the wind at frequencies that can become dangerously self-sustaining.
writing.explanation_ko: 바람에 '수직인(perpendicular)' 방향 — 와류는 건물을 바람이 아닌 옆 방향으로 흔들기 때문.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 각각 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Rectangular skyscrapers create (A)___________ because their shapes are not aerodynamic, and designers use strategies such as orienting the building and modifying corners to (B)___________ the wind and reduce this danger.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 직사각형 형태로 인해 생성되는 것 = "vortices(와류)". (B) 설계자들이 바람에 대해 하는 것 = "disturb(교란하다)" — 강한 와류 형성을 방해.
